page: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized virtual machine engineered for GPU-intensive workloads. The instance couples a dedicated Intel Xeon x86_64 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz with hardware acceleration. Compute resources consist of 12 vCPUs across 6 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, backed by 38 MB of L3 cache, and 85 GB of system memory delivering 7.08 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU equipped with 40 GB of dedicated VRAM. The instance does not include integrated local NVMe storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results highlight an architecture distinctly prioritized around GPU computation rather than raw central processor throughput. The NVIDIA A100 GPU delivers top-tier performance for deep learning inference, processing 8,237 prompt tokens per second and generating 339 tokens per second on small 135M parameter models, alongside 3,469 prompt tokens per second and 150 generation tokens per second on 7B models. In contrast, the Intel Xeon CPU exhibits weak single-core performance with a Geekbench score of 1,060 and a stress-ng score of 1,198.99. Multi-core performance settles in the mid-tier category, reflecting the moderate 6-core allocation, while memory bandwidth achieves 70.62 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads.

The qualitative balance of the a2-highgpu-1g design favors deployments where computation offloads primarily to the GPU subsystem. While the system memory footprint is substantial relative to the vCPU count, the modest single-threaded CPU capability presents a bottleneck for CPU-bound data preprocessing or legacy serial tasks. The lack of complimentary local storage also necessitates external storage planning. This machine configuration is best suited for small to medium large language model inference, computer vision model training, GPU-accelerated batch data transformations, and molecular dynamics simulations.
description: Google Cloud Platform a2-highgpu-1g is an accelerator-optimized instance configured with 12 vCPUs, 6 physical Intel Xeon cores running at 2.2 GHz, 85 GB of system RAM, and a single NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPU with 40 GB of VRAM. It contains no bundled local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier inference speeds for small and medium language models, delivering 3,469 prompt tokens per second on 7B architectures. Conversely, single-threaded CPU throughput is modest, recording bottom-quartile scores across Geekbench and stress-ng tests. Multi-core processing and system memory bandwidth maintain mid-tier marks. Given its concentrated GPU compute density and memory-to-core allocation, the a2-highgpu-1g is an efficient choice for machine learning inference, model fine-tuning, and specialized scientific computing where operations bypass sequential CPU constraints.
